description: Issue #867 (PR #884 cross-vendor review round 2, finding 1) / Issue #1080 refactor: reverts RequestBindingPolicy.Classify's ENTIRE zero-resolution branch body (`if (members.Length == 0) { ... }`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs) to a single `break;` -- reproducing, in the new three-way-split shape, this same mutant id's original move (a single `return false;` reverted to `break;`). Issue #1080 split what used to be that one `if (members.Length == 0) return false;` into three exits: (1) `return UnresolvedIntermediateSegment` for an unresolved INTERMEDIATE segment, (2) `return UnresolvedIntermediateSegment` again, inside a `foreach (var candidate in traversalTypes)` loop, for a LAST segment that resolves against a SHALLOWER type already collected in traversalTypes (a real write is still possible there -- see wtmsec867-nowritabletarget-shallower-candidate-guard-neutralize for the mutant covering that loop directly), and (3) `return NoWritableTarget` for a LAST segment that resolves against nothing in the traversal chain at all. Neutralizing only ONE of those three exits would leave the other two intact and still able to reject both red tests below (both hit exit (1), the intermediate-segment case) -- a half-neutralized guard whose KILLED verdict would misrepresent full coverage as proven when it is not. Replacing the whole block body with `break;` instead makes all three exits simultaneously unreachable in one statement (no leftover unreachable code -- the three `return` statements and their explanatory comments are deleted, not merely made unreachable, which would be CS0162 depending on project settings). `break` exits the `for` loop over `level` immediately and falls through to the trailing `return BindingRejectionReason.None;` (src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs, after the loop) -- the Issue #1080 equivalent of the pre-refactor `return true;` this same mutant id has always modeled: `break` silently allowing the whole key, exactly reproducing the historical PR #884 round 2 bug. (An earlier version of this patch instead neutralized the OUTER `members.Length == 0` condition with a compile-preserving `&& false`, which also disables all three exits as one unit but falls through into `if (members.Length > 1)` / `var member = members[0];` on the now-unguarded EMPTY `members` array -- throwing `System.IndexOutOfRangeException` instead of allowing the key. That shape still got KILLED, but by a crash rather than by the intended `Assert.IsFalse failed` assertion, which does not exercise the same 'guard removed -> silent bypass reaches PropertyHelper.SetPropertyValue' failure mode as the historical bug. The `break;`-body-replacement shape here avoids that: it reproduces an actual silent-allow, not a crash.) Checked against RequestBindingPolicyTests867.IsPathAllowed_MissingIntermediateSegmentThenStaticFinal_ReturnsFalse ('Missing.StaticSecret' -- 'Missing' doesn't resolve on FixtureVM, but 'StaticSecret' does and IS static) and IsPathAllowed_MissingIntermediateSegmentThenAmbiguousFinal_ReturnsFalse ('Missing.Label' against AmbiguousShadowVM, where 'Label' is ambiguous) -- the exact two regression shapes the original review asked for. With the guard reverted, both return BindingRejectionReason.None instead of UnresolvedIntermediateSegment; because IsPathAllowed is a pure delegation to Classify (Issue #1080), IsPathAllowed also returns true instead of false, which is what turns the assertions red -- with a clean `Assert.IsFalse failed.`, not an exception. The green control, IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue, exercises a path where every segment resolves cleanly (members.Length is never 0, so the mutated line is never reached at all) and is genuinely unaffected by this mutant.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.Classify(Type, string, string) -- the entire body of `if (members.Length == 0) { ... }`, now split three ways under Issue #1080's BindingRejectionReason (UnresolvedIntermediateSegment for an unresolved intermediate segment or a last segment resolving against a shallower traversal type; NoWritableTarget for a last segment resolving against nothing) -- reverted as ONE unit to a single `break;`, which falls through the enclosing `for` loop to the trailing `return BindingRejectionReason.None;`
red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against a clean checkout with the regenerated (break-body) mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first), from the TRX <ErrorInfo><Message> node run_mutant.py itself parses: both red tests failed with 'Assert.IsFalse failed. ' (neither test has a custom message, so this is the full MSTest failure text for both, including the trailing space MSTest appends after the period). Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-zero-resolution-guard-neutralize: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS'. (An earlier `&& false`-on-the-outer-condition shape of this same patch instead produced 'Test method ... threw exception: \r\nSystem.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.' for both tests -- reported here only as the reason this entry was regenerated to the break-body shape, not as this entry's current observed text.)
